alt: Looping animation of a hexagonal spiral lattice in orange and violet, two lattice cells across, turning steadily.
caption: The animation this page explains: the published g227 Brusselator orbit in the site's ember palette, 48 frames, exactly one period of 6.390159918584649 time units. Every frame comes from a single forward simulation of the one frame the search found.

alt: Stroboscopic animation, one frame per period. It begins as a sharp spiral lattice, slowly loses contrast over the first third, and ends as an almost flat field blinking in unison.
caption: Why you cannot simply simulate. This starts exactly on the published orbit, disturbed only by single-precision round-off, and simulates forward with the three zero-cost symmetries imposed at every step. One frame per period, 313 periods: the spirals fade, by period 135 none are left, and every point ends up oscillating in unison.
